maya: Quick thread 1: we need a pragmatic rollout for Private packaging upgrades that balances safety and ship velocity. Field wants predictable tenant networking behavior during upgrades.

ryan: Proposal: staged waves by customer risk tier (pilot -> early adopters -> GA). Each wave has a deterministic preflight + dry-run.

nia: From field: key asks are: preserve customer-assigned IPs if possible, avoid tearing BGP sessions, clear maintenance SLAs (max 15m per node), and an operator abort that leaves system in known state.

alejandro: Engineering: we can implement an "interface-preserve" agent mode to skip re-creating tenant interfaces and keep MACs. Work estimate: ~1.5 engineer-weeks + test harness for NIC bounces. Caveat: storage of interface metadata across upgrades.

devx: DX: add installer flags like `--preserve-network=control|full|none` and a `redwoodctl net preflight` that emits a checklist and a pass/fail status. Also surface a telemetry event so we can automatically detect post-upgrade route churn.

ryan: For rollback surface, I suggest a three-step play: (1) pause orchestration, (2) if interface-preserve is on, attempt a local agent rollback that restores old binary + interface state, (3) fallback to redirecting outbound via a regional egress relay (opt-in) if topology is broken.

nia: Field wants the relay option but only with explicit customer consent and bandwidth notes. Also request a customer-facing one-pager describing tradeoffs.

alejandro: Technical note: relay is simple HTTP/TCP proxy; works for outbound but breaks inbound peered connections. We'll document that limitation. Prototype ETA: 4 business days. Harden ETA: 12 business days.

devx: Suggest launch gates: Gate 1: preflight + unit/integration tests (including simulated NIC bounces). Gate 2: internal pilot with 3 customers for 2 maintenance windows. Gate 3: public docs, CLI, rollback runbook, and telemetry dashboards.

maya: Sounds good. Decision for v1: default to `control` (preserve BGP/control-plane, rotate data-plane) to reduce risk and speed GA. Offer `full` as opt-in preview for high-touch customers.

field-bot: Created TICKET-PRIVUP-2107: "Private packaging - network preserve rollout" assigned to maya. Link: https://redwood.internal/TICKET-PRIVUP-2107

maya: Actions: @alejandro scope interface-preserve and relay prototype, @ryan own waves + playbook, @devx add CLI + telemetry, @nia schedule pilots and create customer one-pager. Reconvene in 72h with firm ETAs. :calendar:
